title: A glossary of conceptual histories — read across the breath/pump threshold
note: An authored map, and it says so: a proxy for real histories of meaning and consciousness, carrying its provenance, never the histories themselves. Two regimes of attention are distinguished. BREATH: a participatory, holistic attention whose natural writing is the CONCEPTUAL sign — a symbol holding a weighted field of values at once (the labrys, the ankh, the ouroboros). PUMP: an analytic, segmenting attention whose natural writing is the PHONETIC sign — a mark spelling a sound, deferring meaning to a lexicon (revolution, democracy). The ghost lag is breath-meaning still moving under pump-language, and the cardinal error is phonetic projection: reading a breath-era sign as if it spelled a word. Weighted fields and dated attestations are authored readings; resonance is a proxy for fit to a retained conceptual truth, not proof of what a sign 'really' meant.

concepts.name: Labrys (the Minoan double axe)
concepts.gloss: Not a tool and not a word: a breath-era sign holding, at once and in proportion, a paradoxical equilibrium — opposed blades in balance — with sovereignty, divinity and belonging.

usages.artifact: double-axe motifs incised through the Palace of Knossos and recurring on Minoan seals and larnakes
usages.citation: Evans, The Palace of Minos; the Minoan seal corpus (CMS)
usages.committed_because: to hold and transmit the society's axis — balanced sovereignty, the divine, and belonging — in a form that outlived any one voice and bound everyone who stood under it

usages.quotation: the labrys, sign of the goddess, holds the opposed blades of heaven and earth in balance
usages.citation: after religious-historical studies of Minoan iconography

usages.quotation: the labrys borne as an emblem of sovereign power and the identity of the group
usages.citation: after later political and heraldic adoptions of the double axe

concepts.name: Ankh (the Egyptian sign of life)
concepts.gloss: Literally the breath of life: carried in the hand of gods, held to the nostrils of the king. A conceptual sign whose whole content is living continuity given and divine.

usages.artifact: the ankh held by deities and offered to the king's nostrils in tomb and temple relief
usages.citation: New Kingdom tomb and temple reliefs
usages.committed_because: to make the gift of life itself visible and transmissible beyond the spoken blessing — a thing too profound to leave to word of mouth

concepts.name: Ouroboros (the tail-eating serpent)
concepts.gloss: The serpent that consumes its own tail: cyclical unity, the paradox of consumption and renewal held as one totality.

usages.artifact: the encircling serpent around the sun-god in the Enigmatic Book of the Netherworld
usages.citation: Tomb of Tutankhamun, the Enigmatic Book of the Netherworld
usages.committed_because: to set down the wholeness of time's return — end as beginning — in a single form that a culture could carry across generations

usages.quotation: the ouroboros, hen to pan — the one is the all — the serpent devouring and renewing itself end to end
usages.citation: the Greco-Egyptian alchemical corpus (the Chrysopoeia of Kleopatra)

usages.quotation: the ouroboros borne upon the device, a serpent in a ring, token of an unending line
usages.citation: after late-medieval heraldry and emblem books

usages.quotation: the ouroboros, slaying and wedding and renewing itself, the One that is the All — a symbol of the integration of opposites
usages.citation: after Jung, on the ouroboros as a symbol of wholeness

concepts.name: Divine order (myth as conceptual memory)
concepts.gloss: Myth read not as report but as memory: a remembered state-shift, embedded enough to keep its place, lifted up a ladder of abstraction — elemental forces, then primal powers, then ordered Olympians, then allegory — each form making the memory more transmissible.

senses.label: the elements as living powers
senses.gloss: sky, earth, sea, storm attended as living forces — not yet persons, not yet named

senses.label: primal/chthonic powers, personified
senses.gloss: the older generation — Titans, chthonic powers — the forces given face and lineage

senses.label: the ordered Olympian pantheon
senses.gloss: anthropomorphic persons in a ruled cosmos — the memory organised into a court

senses.label: gods as allegories of forces
senses.gloss: the gods read as personified virtues and forces — philosophy's segmenting reduction of the memory

usages.quotation: This Theogony sings how, at the first, Chaos came to be, and next wide-bosomed Earth, and the succession of the powers
usages.committed_because: to fix in lasting, phonetic form a breath-era memory of how the powers came to be — written down precisely at the threshold, so the memory would not be lost as the mode of attention changed

concepts.name: Revolution
concepts.gloss: A pump-regime word whose concept inverted: from a turning-back to a breaking-forward. The phonetic contrast to the breath-era signs above.

senses.label: cyclical return (astronomical)
senses.gloss: the revolving of the heavenly spheres back through their course; a cyclical, lawful return to the starting point

senses.label: return to a prior rightful order
senses.gloss: a turning-back in politics: the restoration of an ancient, legitimate order that had been usurped

senses.label: irreversible forward rupture
senses.gloss: a fundamental, irreversible break that founds a wholly new order and cannot be turned back — the meaning inverted

senses.label: any profound, rapid transformation
senses.gloss: the sense loosed from politics onto any sweeping change: industrial, scientific, digital revolution

usages.quotation: the late happy Revolution, whereby our ancient laws and liberties were restored to us
usages.citation: English political pamphlet, c. 1689 (the Glorious Revolution)

usages.quotation: the Revolution is not a return but the beginning of a wholly new age, from which there is no going back
usages.citation: after the French Revolutionary press, c. 1791

concepts.name: Democracy
concepts.gloss: A pump-regime word whose standing rose: from a term of abuse for mob-rule to an honorific ideal.

senses.label: rule by the unqualified many (pejorative)
senses.gloss: in classical political theory, the deviant form of popular rule — government by the many in their own narrow interest, prone to disorder

senses.label: legitimate popular self-government (honorific)
senses.gloss: self-rule by the people as a legitimate, even ideal, form of government — the standing of the word reversed

usages.quotation: demokratia, the rule of the demos, is counted the deviant form, prone to disorder
democracy is the gradual development of the equality of conditions, a providential fact to which all must adapt
